title: Verifier–Agent Co-Design to Reduce Verifier Tax in Agentic NetOps Planning (provisional preregistration)
research_question: Does runtime verifier feedback integrated into LLM planning (co-design) reduce verifier-induced blocking of safe plans and increase safe end-to-end completion rate relative to a static post-hoc verifier, without materially increasing planning latency, across multiple NetOps task classes (routing, ACL, VLAN) in a deterministic emulated testbed?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (primary): The co-design condition (runtime verifier feedback) yields a higher safe end-to-end completion rate than the static post-hoc verifier condition (paired difference > 0).
H2: Co-design does not increase median planning latency by more than 20% relative to static verification (non-inferiority margin: 20%).
exploratory_questions: E1: How do verifier interventions (counts, types) differ by task class (routing, ACL, VLAN)?
E2: How sensitive are outcomes to verifier-feedback intensity (three deterministic levels)?
E3: What failure-mode distributions (syntax, semantic-mismatch, unsafe execution) differ between conditions?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic intent→configuration NetOps task corpus (three task classes: routing, ACL, VLAN) generated by the published generator with fixed seeds
Deterministic containerized emulator images (two topology classes: small spine-leaf and medium enterprise) as provided
Evaluation strictly bounded to the supplied synthetic/emulated testbed and published task generator
secondary_estimands: distributional differences in failure-mode proportions by task class
sampling_plan: Paired design. Each unique task instance is executed twice (once under Static post-hoc verifier (baseline) and once under Co-design runtime verifier feedback (guarded)), forming one paired observation. Task corpus: 2 topology classes × per-topology task instances = 200 paired tasks (exact). Inclusion: tasks produced by the published task-generator script using provided seeds. Exclusion: tasks whose emulator setup fails deterministically (see retry policy). Randomization: task ordering randomized with fixed seed 42 for execution order only; pairing preserved. Retry policy: up to 2 automated infra-retries for transient emulator or API failures; if a retry succeeds both runs of the pair are kept; if retries exhaust and one condition completed while the other failed, pair is marked incomplete and excluded from the primary analysis (complete-pair primary). Sensitivity: secondary analysis treats incomplete pairs as failed (success=0) for guarded and baseline as described in analysis plan.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: absolute paired difference = 0.10. Calculation method: normal-approximation paired-proportion power calculation with conservative variance estimate and assumed within-task correlation ρ = 0.5. Power target 80%, two-sided α=0.05. Assumptions: baseline safe completion rate assumed 0.60, ρ=0.5. Recommended scenario: S2_recommended_moderate equivalent (N=200 paired tasks). Sensitivity analyses will recompute MDE over baseline p in {0.4,0.5,0.6,0.7} and ρ in {0.2,0.5,0.8}.
exclusion_rules: Exclude pairs where emulator configuration hash mismatches declared topology image hash (infra-failure).
Exclude pairs where deterministic parser reports syntax error on generated DSL.
Exclude contaminated items flagged by deterministic pre-lock-hash comparison (see contamination_plan).
Incomplete pairs (one condition failed after retry policy) excluded from primary analysis; reported in full.
missingness_plan: Primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs (complete_pair_primary). Automated retry policy as specified in sampling_plan. Sensitivity analysis reinterprets any incomplete pair as a failed success (0) in both conditions for conservative bounds. All exclusions and number of incomplete pairs reported with deterministic reasons (infra-failure, API quota, deterministic emulator error). No human adjudication permitted; treatments are deterministic and logged.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis executed by registered analysis contract 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' computing estimand 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline' (primary_estimand_id). Primary dataset: all complete pairs (both conditions produced final execution outcome within retry policy). Primary test: two-sided paired test (contract implementation will use exact paired test or its internal preferred exact method); report mean paired difference with 95% CI and exact counts. Failed-call treatment for primary: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude incomplete pairs). Sensitivity analysis: 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' — incomplete pairs counted as failures (success=0). Secondary analyses: paired median latency ratio (report nonparametric effect size), verifier-block-rate difference, and stratified analyses by task class. Holm-Bonferroni correction applied across secondary estimands; exploratory contrasts reported as exploratory.
multiplicity_plan: One pre-registered primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference). Apply Holm-Bonferroni correction across secondary estimands. Exploratory analyses reported without confirmatory p-value thresholds and explicitly labelled exploratory.

stopping_rule: Stop when all 200 paired tasks complete under retry policy and deterministic validity checks, or upon reaching the adapter's maximum_model_calls (400), or upon exceeding the capability_manifest maximum_wall_clock_days (7 days). If persistent provider or infrastructure outage prevents completion within retries or wall-clock cap, halt and report incomplete pairs per missingness_plan.
